correctness.rationale: The underlying 24-edge cubic graph is given explicitly. Independent exact enumeration of all 8-edge perfect matchings found 33 matchings, and exhaustive disjoint-matching triples yielded exactly 20 distinct unordered proper colourings. Full two-factor cycle switching gives 27 undirected edges and component orders 16 and 4; it yields profiles 16 times ((6,10),(6,10),(6,10)), 3 times ((8,8),(16),(16)), and once ((8,8),(8,8),(8,8)). The supplied explicit index-to-GP(8,3) vertex map was separately checked: its 24 image edges equal exactly the 24 definition edges and it bijects the 16 large-component vertices. The small component is the 3-leaf star, with center state 1. The first-uncovered-vertex matching recursion, all matching partitions, and alternating component switches cover all finite possibilities; this is an exhaustive finite proof, not extrapolation. Graph vertex labels are held fixed and only global colour names are factored out.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is a canonical symmetric nonplanar cubic graph, and the full reconfiguration structure of its proper edge-colourings is a natural invariant; the nontrivial self-reproduction of the original graph as one component and distinct four-state claw, plus exact bichromatic profiles, is mathematically more informative than a scalar class count. This complete finite structural classification can serve as a benchmark for edge-Kempe equivalence graph theory without purporting to yield an infinite-family theorem.
